question: The National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) was initiated in the ________ Five-Year Plan.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sixth Five-Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Rural Employment Programme (NREP)** was launched in **October 1980** during the **Sixth Five-Year Plan**. It was designed to replace the earlier **Food for Work Programme** to streamline employment generation in rural sectors.
 
• The primary objective of the **NREP** was to generate additional gainful employment for the unemployed and underemployed persons in the rural areas of **India**.
 
• This programme aimed at the creation of **durable community assets** for strengthening the rural infrastructure, such as **rural roads**, **school buildings**, and **panchayat ghars**.
 
• The funding for the **National Rural Employment Programme** was shared between the **Central Government** and the **State Governments** on a **50:50** basis.
 
• Under this initiative, a specific target was set to generate **300 to 400 million mandays** of employment per annum for the rural poor to ensure food security and income stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–1985):**
 
 
• The **Sixth Five-Year Plan** marked the beginning of economic liberalization in **India** and focused heavily on **poverty alleviation** and **economic self-reliance**.
 
• The plan was launched under the leadership of **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi** with a target growth rate of **5.2%**, but it successfully achieved a growth rate of **5.7%**.
 
• It emphasized **family planning** to control the growing **population** and invested significantly in the **energy sector** and **agriculture**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Employment Schemes:**
 
 
• In **1983**, during the same plan period, the **Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP)** was introduced to provide a guarantee of employment to at least one member of every landless household for up to **100 days** in a **year**.
 
• Later, on **April 1, 1989**, both **NREP** and **RLEGP** were merged to form the **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY)**, which became a major flagship employment scheme.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–1978):**
 
 
• This plan focused on **'Garibi Hatao'** (Removal of Poverty) and **Justice**. It was terminated **one year** early in **1978** by the **Janata Party government**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP)** was another crucial scheme launched in **1980** to provide self-employment opportunities to the rural poor through **subsidies** and **bank loans**.
 
• The **National Rural Employment Programme** prioritized the **Scheduled Castes (SC)** and **Scheduled Tribes (ST)** for employment, ensuring that a portion of the funds was reserved for their **socio-economic development**.
 
• The **Sixth Plan** is often cited as the **'Plan of Infrastructure'** as it significantly expanded **irrigation projects** and **national highways** across the **country**.
 
• Currently, the spirit of these early employment programmes is carried forward by the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, which was enacted in **2005** to provide a legal **Right to Work**.
